name: norvel
author: music-rhythm-and-dance agent
description:
norvel (direction: music, rhythm and dance) - A DRUM-MACHINE GRID, AND THE HOLES THE SNARE FILLS
EXACTLY. PRIVATE; never shown to players.

CLUE = "<kick>/<n>". <kick> is one drum row of 16/20/24/28 steps over "x" (a hit) and "." (a rest);
it always starts and ends with a hit and has G = 4..8 maximal HOLES (maximal runs of "."), each
1-5 steps, at most one of length 1, at least one of length >= 3, at least two distinct lengths.
n is 2..5 and G = n + 1..4, so n is never the number of holes (the complement of the clue is
therefore always wrong) and never the number of kick runs, the number of kick hits or the longest
hole.

SOLUTION = a drum-machine picture. The scorer deletes every character that is not "x" or ".", drops
empty lines, and requires EXACTLY THREE rows, all as long as the clue, with the FIRST row equal to
the clue. Labels ("kick"/"snare"/"hat", "bd"/"sn"/"hh", "1"/"2"/"3", ...), bar lines "|", a beat-number
header, spaces, tabs and blank lines are all free - the grader reads only the x/. skeleton.
THE RULE: exactly n of the maximal runs of "x" in the SECOND row have exactly the same span
(same first step AND same last step) as a hole of the clue row. "The snare fills n of the kick's
holes exactly - no more, no less." The third row is free and is where "any drum will do" dies.

INTENDED DISCOVERY PATH. (a) it is a drum grid and the top line is the clue - round 1 from one demo;
(b) the second row is what counts, not the third (every demo has the third row exactly filling a
different number of holes); (c) something about the snare and the kick's holes - the demo headline;
(d) EXACTLY, not "inside" and not "over" - forced by the near-misses in every demo. (d) decides
the run. Kid sentence a 12-year-old can say from one demo: "the snare fills up two of the kick's
holes exactly - it starts the beat the kick stops and stops the beat the kick comes back".

DEMO GUARANTEES (measured, 1200 demos): a counted fill >= 3 steps long 100 %; a "too long" run
that covers a whole hole and spills over a kick hit 100 %; a "too short" run strictly inside a
hole 65.9 % (structurally impossible when only one hole is left over); a run as long as a hole but
in the wrong place 89.4 %; the third row exactly fills a different number of holes 100 %. 22 rival
counters (runs, hits, holes touched, holes covered, columns with k hits, unison hits, row-3
versions, clue-only readings) are checked per demo and essentially never equal n (worst 19.6 %
"holes the third row covers", i.e. 6e-5 over six demos; every other rival <= 3.1 %). solve() randomises the fill set, the near-misses, the third row, the
instrument names, the bar lines and the header, and never emits the minimal witness.

DEGENERATE WITNESSES CLOSED (800 fresh clues each): empty / junk / clue echoed / 4000 chars 0.00 %;
copy the clue row three times 0.00 %; clue + two empty or two full rows 0.00 %; a well-formed random
picture 0.04-0.62 %; THE COMPLEMENT (fill every hole exactly) 0.00 % by construction (n < G);
complement minus one hole 34.6 %, minus two 27.6 %, "always fill exactly k holes" 29-30 % - these
are the CEILING, and each needs the whole insight (a run must MATCH a hole) and only misses what n
means (G - n is spread over 1..4 on purpose, so no constant guess pays more than ~35 %); grafting an
old answer's rows 2-3 under the new clue row 1.9 % (1.1 % from a demo with the same n); demo replay
on the next clue 0.00 %; one fixed answer for every clue 0.12 %; right rule in row 3 instead of
row 2 0.56 %; rows 2/3 swapped 0.00 %; n holes covered with a spill 0.00 %; n unison hits on the
kick 0.00 %; exactly n snare runs anywhere 0.17 %. FOOTHOLD (DESIGN_LOOP lever 7): the natural loose
reading "put a run inside n of the holes" scores 7.5 % (flush-left variant 8.6 %, one hit per hole
0.0 %), so partial insight is paid without giving the rule away.

FAIRNESS. Over a family of 141 "count a relation in the picture" counters the demos leave
12.2 -> 4.4 -> 1.9 -> 1.5 -> 1.1 -> 1.0 survivors after 1..6 demos, and the last survivor is the
true rule in 12/12 trials: the difficulty is generating the hypothesis, not testing it. Scorer:
0 raises and 0 non-binary answers on 63 000 junk strings (worst 0.49 ms), 0 disagreements with an
independent re-implementation on 10 400 mutated answers, solve() scores 1 on 1500/1500 fresh clues
and on 2000 more, generate deterministic on 3000 seeds (0.03 ms mean, 0.14 ms worst), solve 12 ms
mean / 52 ms worst. Whitespace, bar lines, labels, a beat header, blank lines, tabs and CRLF are
all accepted; rows reversed, rows 2/3 swapped, 2 or 4 rows, or one wrong character in the clue row
all score 0.

LEVERS. Too easy: count only holes >= 2 long; require the third row to be silent through a counted
hole; name the counted row in the clue. Too hard: add the number of holes as a second clue field;
guarantee three fills >= 3 long per demo; drop the third row.
